titulo: Cache and idle time: what the October numbers show
lead: Going back to a large session that has sat idle for two hours can cost hundreds of thousands of tokens in a single message. It's not a bug: the cache expired. With the numbers measured in October 2026, you'll understand the timeline of an idle session and decide, with real math, between resending and starting clean.
objetivo: read the timeline of an idle session (45, 54, 60 min) and choose between resending and /clear + /prime using the measured numbers.

aprende.t: What happens at 45, ~54 and 60 min idle
The measured numbers: cache, compactions and resumption
The gate that holds the first message after the pause
When to resend and when to /clear + /prime

hero_alt: Glass hourglass on a dark circuit board, with a digital thermometer beside it.

secoes.titulo: The timeline of an idle session
secoes.sub: Claude Code, 1 h cache, context above ~200k tokens, hook-longrun 1.9.6 on.

nos.detalhe: On the Stop event, with context ≥ 200k and the handoffs/ folder in the project, the hook schedules a timer (systemd-run --user, one per session, reset on every response). If you send another message, the clock starts over.

If you switch focus, Claude Code writes an away_summary into the conversation. Since 1.8.6 this (and local commands like /exit) no longer counts as "the session moved": before, 7 sessions on 10/16 were left without a handoff because of it.

If the session is still idle, with no handoff from this session saved within 5 min of the last reply, and the cache is still valid (< 55 min), the hook saves the handoff on a COPY of the session: same model, warm cache, allowed to run only handoff-grava.py and read files. The open session is not touched.

Claude Code compacts on its own after about 55 min without a reply, only above ~200k tokens, before the cache expires. In the records from Oct 7 to 15, 2026, all 93 compactions came 53–58 min after the last reply. But it doesn't always happen: on Oct 18, a 480k session did not compact.

The next message rereads the whole conversation with no cache. With more than 150k in context, the hook holds that first message once and explains: resending continues; /clear + /prime starts clean from this session's handoff.

secoes.legenda: Why 45 and not 50: idle-time compaction comes between 53 and 58 min, and the copy takes 30–60 s plus startup. At 45 there's some slack; the cost is the same at any time before 1 h.

rolagem_fim.texto: Compaction is a bonus when it comes. The handoff at 45 min, saved while the cache is warm, is what guarantees the return has a cheap path.

secoes.sub: All from the execucao-longa kit, with the date and sample size.

texto: With a warm cache (up to ~1 h since the last reply), rereading the conversation costs ~10% of the input price. Expired, it reprocesses everything and writes the cache again, ~2×: about 20× a message with a warm cache.
On a subscription this doesn't turn into money, but it comes out of the 5 h and weekly quota. And you pay once: the following messages are cheap again.
Resending with an expired cache: median of 284k token-equivalents on the first call (190 cases, from 17k to 1.25 million) and ~23k per turn afterward.
/clear + /prime: median of 187k (only 11 cases) and ~10k per turn afterward. The floor comes from rewriting the initial package (instructions, memory, skills).

exemplo.texto: Some of the 190 resumptions may have gone through compaction before; /prime has only 11 cases.

passos.titulo: The cache is not the problem
texto: Between 93% and 99% cache in every long session measured, with no decline as compactions pile up. It's no reason to cut the session short.
What grows is the cost per turn: without compacting, the last tenth of a 1M session read ~5× more per turn than the first (810k versus 157k).
If the decisions are in files (commits, state.md, handoff), /clear + /prime is cheaper from then on.
Resending and paying for the full reread only makes sense when a decision lives only in the conversation and didn't make it into the handoff.

secoes.sub: Same ensaio-hook.sh from lesson 3: fake transcript with 220k tokens and the last reply 120 min ago.

blocos.conteudo:
rm -rf /tmp/ensaio-hook
bash ensaio-hook.sh 220000 120 UserPromptSubmit   # 1ª mensagem depois da pausa
bash ensaio-hook.sh - - UserPromptSubmit          # reenviar a mesma
bash ensaio-hook.sh 250000 0 Stop                 # fim de resposta: agenda o handoff por ociosidade
cat /tmp/ensaio-hook/agenda.jsonl

blocos.rot: Hook variables (in the Claude Code environment)
blocos.conteudo:
LONGRUN_PAUSA_MIN=60          # minutos parado antes de segurar a mensagem
LONGRUN_PAUSA_TOKENS=150000   # contexto mínimo para segurar; 0 desliga a trava
LONGRUN_OCIOSO_MIN=45         # minutos parado antes de gravar o handoff (não passe de ~45)
LONGRUN_OCIOSO_TOKENS=200000  # contexto mínimo para gravar; 0 desliga
LONGRUN_CACHE_MIN=55          # depois disso a cópia não roda (o cache já estaria frio)

abas.html:
$ bash ensaio-hook.sh 220000 120 UserPromptSubmit
{"decision": "block", "reason": "Sessão parada há 2h00: o cache venceu e esta mensagem
 vai reprocessar ~220 mil tokens do seu limite. Para continuar aqui, reenvie a mensagem.
 Para começar limpo: NENHUM handoff desta sessão foi gravado: antes do /clear, peça para
 gravar (skill session-handoff), senão o /prime não terá o caminho deste trabalho."}

$ bash ensaio-hook.sh - - UserPromptSubmit

$ bash ensaio-hook.sh 250000 0 Stop

$ cat /tmp/ensaio-hook/agenda.jsonl
{"unidade": "longrun-ocioso-ensaio", "minutos": 45, "cmd": ["/usr/bin/python3",
 ".../execucao-longa/tools/hook-longrun.py", "--ocioso", "ensaio", ...]}

With LONGRUN_AGENDAR_ARQ the hook only records the scheduling in a file, instead of creating the real timer. It's the same variable the kit's tests use.

Example from the kit's README (session idle for 5h33 with 220k tokens):

● UserPromptSubmit operation blocked by hook:
  Sessão parada há 5h33: o cache venceu e esta mensagem vai reprocessar ~220 mil tokens do seu limite.
  Para continuar aqui, reenvie a mensagem. Para começar limpo: /clear e depois /prime
  (o último handoff do projeto é indicado na abertura).

Since 1.7.1, when this session saved a handoff, the warning includes its path on separate lines: /clear and /prime handoffs/history/[file].md. Another session may have saved a newer one in the same project.

secoes.sub: Rehearsal at no cost, and a tweak that protects your transcripts.

exercicios.texto: Run the 2-hour pause block. Then run it with 90000 tokens instead of 220000, in a clean folder, to see the 150k limit.
exercicios.pronto: the 1st call prints "decision": "block" with cache venceu; the resend (-) prints nothing; with 90k there is no block; agenda.jsonl shows "minutos": 45.

exercicios.texto: Claude Code deletes transcripts after cleanupPeriodDays (default 30). Without them, there is no measurement and no recall (lesson 7). Set 365 in settings.json.

perguntas.p: Why does the hook write the handoff on idle time at 45 min, and not at 58?
opcoes: Because at 45 min the cache has already expired and the copy has to run before the automatic compaction
To land before the idle-time compaction and the end of the cache, leaving room for the copy
perguntas.explica: Writing with a warm cache costs one cheap read. At 50 the copy may arrive after the summary or go past the 55 min cache limit. Whoever is working is not interrupted: the copy runs separately.

perguntas.p: In the October measurements, the cache of long sessions...
opcoes: dropped a little with each compaction, because the new summary invalidates the prefix
stayed between 93% and 99% and did not get worse with compactions
perguntas.explica: 93–99% in every long session measured. What grows without compaction is the cost per turn (~5× in the last tenth), not the loss of cache.

perguntas.p: Session idle for 3 h, 300k tokens, all decisions already in this session's handoff. What to do on return?
opcoes: Resend the message: with 300k tokens already loaded, it's always the cheapest
perguntas.explica: With the path in a file, starting clean costs less from then on (~10k × ~23k per turn, measured through 10/17). Resending only pays off if something lived only in the conversation.

perguntas.p: The pause gate blocked your message. You want to continue in this session. What to do?
opcoes: Run /compact first, so the session fits in the cache and the gate lifts
Wait for the cache to come back
Resend the same message: the block applies once per pause
perguntas.explica: The block is a question, not an error: it applies once per pause and is saved in the session state. Resending goes straight through.

itens.texto: Handoff on the copy with a warm cache, idle-time compaction when it comes, expired cache and the gate on return.
Cache 93–99% (10/01); resume 284k × 187k and ~23k × ~10k per turn (14 days through 10/17).
Path in a file: /clear + /prime. Something only in the conversation: resend once and write the handoff.
